obs1000: Interior floor, inner walls and the inside end wall are all a single near-black value. 1000-top is one undifferentiated black slab: the floor cannot be told from the walls, and only the thin wall-thickness rim and the two block stubs give it shape. This is the direct cause of the slab/graphic reading in the whole model.

The exterior walls are clean uniform tan right up to the torn rim, apart from slight soft darkening near the break in 1000-rear-three-quarter. The tan-to-black boundary at the rim is therefore a hard silhouette value step. In 1000-right this becomes the jagged zig-zag graphic.
The torn contour is a fairly regular sawtooth. It is designed rather than measured, and I accept that as stated.

The two inboard mounting blocks read as attached supports (top view: flush stubs; left and rear-three-quarter: cast shadows land on the wall). They are not floating debris. Their pure black against tan reads as graphic squares.
1000-front shows a thin vertical line near x 724 and dark sliver strokes along the right edge, consistent with wall-thickness edges seen edge-on. Minor.
partFindingsVerbatim.obs256: The open box reads in both three-quarter views. The top view is still a black slab.
partFindingsVerbatim.obs128: Reads as a tan box with a black top. The zig-zag survives in the right view as a graphic band.
partFindingsVerbatim.floorVsWallRoles: JUSTIFIED and, for readability, NECESSARY before any future bake. Proposal: a matte floor role with a lighter ash/residue value and high roughness; soot near-black walls; optionally a narrow heat-darkened band on the exterior below the torn rim, so the rim boundary is not a pure tan/black step. This follows the ash and residue categories in Hansen and Doha (lighter debris on lower surfaces; blackened box sides with hard-edged paint loss). It does not copy their colors. It is a material-role assignment within the existing UVs. It is not a geometry rebuild and not a whole palette retry.
